c74object.name: syncSuite.video.context
c74object.digest: Video rendering context. Wrapper around jit.world for easier and extended functionalities.
c74object.description: It allows out-of-the-box advanced video output, including compositing and exact-pixel mapping. syncSuite.video.context works seemlessly with the SyncSuite package and Max4Live devices.

inlet.digest: Messages controlling the context, plus every jit.world message/attribute
inlet.description: Accepts the "projectionMode", "cameraContext" and "context" messages described below. Anything else is passed straight through to the underlying jit.world, so all of jit.world's own messages and attributes (e.g. "enable", "visible", "size", "fps", "erase_color", "preserve_aspect", "floating", "displaylink", "fsaa", "fsmenubar", "border", "dim", "transparency", "drawto") work exactly as they do on jit.world itself, and can be set at creation as "@attr value" too.

outlet.digest: jit.world's matrix output, when @outputmatrix is enabled
outlet.description: Outputs the rendered content as a jit_matrix, but only while jit.world's @outputmatrix attribute is on (off by default).
Outputs a bang once per rendered frame, at the context's configured @fps.
Outputs "<width> <height>" whenever the window's pixel size changes.

objarg.name: context
objarg.description: Required. Names the shared Jitter OpenGL context created by this object; other Jitter GL objects, and syncSuite.video.source's @context attribute, must reference this same name to render into it. Can be changed later with the "context" message.

method.name: projectionMode
method.digest: Switches between UV space and pixel space
method.description: 0 (default) renders in OpenGL's normalized UV space: resolution-agnostic and relative to the texture, with position 0. 0. always centered in the window - well suited to video-mapping with a projector. 1 renders in pixel space: the texture occupies its exact size in pixels on the canvas, with position 0 0 aligned to the canvas's top-left pixel - well suited to mapping a single screen or multiple screens/LED walls. Pixel space is rendered through a second, internal camera and a custom shader kept in sync with the window's live pixel size; enabling "projectionMode" is what turns that camera on. A paired syncSuite.video.source must independently be set to the same projectionMode to actually draw in that space.

method.name: cameraContext
method.digest: Redirects the pixel-space camera to another context
method.description: By default the internal pixel-space camera draws into this object's own master context. Sending "cameraContext" retargets it to draw into a different named context (typically a jit.gl.node), decoupling pixel-space rendering from the master context even while "projectionMode" is 1. This lets pixel-space and UV-space layers be composited separately before being combined in the master context - point a syncSuite.video.source at that node's name (via its @context attribute) to have it render into that decoupled pixel-space layer.

method.name: context
method.description: Changes this object's own master rendering context name at runtime, same role as the creation argument.

attribute.name: cameraContext
attribute.digest: Context the pixel-space camera draws into

attribute.name: visible
attribute.digest: Shows or hides the window (jit.world attribute)

attribute.name: erase_color
attribute.description: Forwarded to jit.world, as RGBA floats 0.-1. Default 0. 0. 0. 1.

attribute.name: preserve_aspect
attribute.digest: Preserves aspect ratio on resize (jit.world attribute)

attribute.name: displaylink
attribute.digest: Syncs rendering to the display refresh (jit.world attribute)

attribute.name: fsmenubar
attribute.digest: Shows the menu bar in fullscreen (jit.world attribute)

attribute.name: border
attribute.digest: Shows the window's title bar/border (jit.world attribute)

c74object.discussion: syncSuite.video.context wraps jit.world: any attribute or message not listed above (e.g. "dim", "transparency", "drawto", "title"...) is passed straight through to the underlying jit.world unchanged, so the full jit.world reference applies here too. By itself, the object renders nothing useful - it exists to be paired with one or more syncSuite.video.source (and syncSuite.video.subs) instances that target its name via their own @context attribute. See the syncSuite.video.source reference for how projection modes are set on the source side.
